primitives.name: Fabricated Data Guardrail
primitives.verbatim_quote: **No fabricated data on customer surfaces.** Every customer-facing page that shows a record, win-rate, or claim must source it from `evaluatePublicPerformancePolicy()` in `apps/web/lib/performance/public-performance-policy.ts` (or be server-side gated by `getReadinessGates()`).
primitives.assumptions: All customer-facing data originates from a deterministic policy evaluation or is gated by readiness logic.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When D ∉ P or ¬S, data integrity is compromised.

layer2.mapping: Customer data integrity maps to a policy-checking automaton in GSI; GSE enforces readiness gates as state transitions.
layer2.telemetry: CI failure on unauthorized data exposure.

primitives.name: Banned Phrase Registry
primitives.verbatim_quote: **No banned phrases on public copy.** The trust-claim registry in `apps/web/lib/trust-claims.ts` lists every banned phrase.
primitives.assumptions: Every public copy is checked against a static registry of prohibited language.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When F ∈ R, T evaluates to false.

layer2.mapping: Registry-based filtering in GSI mirrors kernel-level input sanitization in GSE.
layer2.telemetry: CI test failure on banned phrase detection.

primitives.name: Bootstrap Pick Isolation
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Bootstrap picks never count toward public performance.** Pick queries that feed customer surfaces must include `isBootstrap: false`.
primitives.assumptions: Only non-bootstrap picks contribute to public performance records.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When B = true, P is excluded from C.

layer2.mapping: Bootstrap isolation in GSI corresponds to data exclusion in GSE’s state transition engine.

Fabricated data guardrails ensure that all public-facing data is derived from verifiable policies. Banned phrase registries act as linguistic filters that prevent reputational risk. Bootstrap pick isolation prevents synthetic data skewing performance metrics. Together, they constitute a formalized epistemological barrier against misinformation and unauthorized publishing. Each primitive operates under a shared invariant: public exposure requires explicit validation. Failure modes include bypassing policy checks, introducing banned language, or including bootstrap data in public views. These are detected via CI enforcement and runtime telemetry.
